Fixed-date Christian feasts through the.Epiphany: Celebrated twelve days after Christmas, it marks the visit of the Magi, and in many Spanish-speaking countries, it is the day children get gifts.
Fixed-date Christian feasts through the.Candlemas: Forty days after Christmas, with candles blessed that day, and it is tied to the weather lore behind Groundhog Day.
Fixed-date Christian feasts through the.Annunciation: Nine months before Christmas, it was also Lady Day, the start of the legal new year in England until 1752.
Fixed-date Christian feasts through the.Nativity of John the Baptist: Placed about six months before Christmas, near the summer solstice, which is why many places light midsummer bonfires on its eve.
Fixed-date Christian feasts through the.Transfiguration: Recalls the moment Jesus appeared radiant on a mountain beside Moses and Elijah, a scene painted by Raphael.
Fixed-date Christian feasts through the.Assumption of Mary: A public holiday in many countries, including France and Italy, where Ferragosto is a mid-August summer break.
Fixed-date Christian feasts through the.Holy Cross Day: It marks the traditional finding of the True Cross by Helena, mother of Constantine, and is a major feast in Eastern churches.
Fixed-date Christian feasts through the.Michaelmas: In England the day was a quarter day, when rents were due, and eating goose was a long-standing custom.
Fixed-date Christian feasts through the.Immaculate Conception: Often mistaken for Jesus' conception, it actually concerns Mary's own conception, and is a public holiday in Spain and Italy.
Fixed-date Christian feasts through the.Christmas: The Bible never gives the date of Jesus' birth, and 25 December appears in a Roman calendar from the 4th century.

Lengths of famous canals.Corinth Canal: This ship canal slices through rock up to 79 meters high and saves ships a trip of roughly 700 km around the Peloponnese.
Lengths of famous canals.Cape Cod Canal: A shortcut of roughly 135 miles around Cape Cod's dangerous shoals opened in 1914.
Lengths of famous canals.Welland Canal: It carries ships around Niagara Falls from Lake Erie to Lake Ontario, lifting them about 99 meters through a series of locks.
Lengths of famous canals.Manchester Ship Canal: Opened in 1894, it turned inland Manchester into a major seaport, and its construction was one of the great engineering feats of Victorian Britain.
Lengths of famous canals.Panama Canal: Opened in 1914, the canal lifts ships about 26 meters up to Gatun Lake, saving a trip around Cape Horn.
Lengths of famous canals.Kiel Canal: Linking the North Sea and the Baltic, it is often described as the world's busiest artificial waterway by number of ships.
Lengths of famous canals.Suez Canal: Opened in 1869, it was blocked for six days in 2021 when the container ship Ever Given ran aground.
Lengths of famous canals.Canal du Midi: Pierre-Paul Riquet built this link between the Atlantic and Mediterranean in the 17th century. It is a World Heritage site.
Lengths of famous canals.Erie Canal: Opened in 1825, it made New York the nation's leading port and was nicknamed 'Clinton's Ditch'.
Lengths of famous canals.Grand Canal, China: The oldest and longest canal in the world links Beijing and Hangzhou, and some stretches date back over 2,000 years.

When these ancient ruins were first buil.Çatalhöyük: This Neolithic town in Turkey had houses crammed together with no streets, entered by ladders through the roofs.
When these ancient ruins were first buil.Newgrange: This Irish tomb predates Stonehenge and the pyramids, and at the winter solstice a shaft of sunlight floods its inner chamber.
When these ancient ruins were first buil.Mohenjo-daro: An Indus Valley city with planned grid streets, covered drains and a Great Bath, whose script remains undeciphered.
When these ancient ruins were first buil.Palace of Knossos: The Minoan palace on Crete may have inspired the Minotaur's labyrinth legend, and Arthur Evans dug it up in 1900.
When these ancient ruins were first buil.Lion Gate of Mycenae: Two lionesses guard the entrance in what is one of Europe's oldest monumental sculptures.
When these ancient ruins were first buil.Persepolis: The Persian ceremonial capital was burned in 330 BC by Alexander's army.
When these ancient ruins were first buil.Hadrian's Wall: The Roman wall stretches 73 miles across northern England and was lined with forts and milecastles.
When these ancient ruins were first buil.Sigiriya rock fortress: A palace on a 180-meter granite rock in Sri Lanka, with cliffside frescoes of women, built by King Kasyapa.
When these ancient ruins were first buil.Tikal Temple I: Tikal's temple rises out of the Guatemalan jungle, and the site was used as the rebel base in the original Star Wars.
When these ancient ruins were first buil.Great Zimbabwe: Its huge stone walls were laid without mortar, and the modern country of Zimbabwe takes its name from the site.

Landmark laptops.Osborne 1: Its 11 kg bundle was called portable and bundled in software, but the company went bankrupt in 1983.
Landmark laptops.GRiD Compass: Its clamshell design with a flip-up screen was used on the Space Shuttle, and it cost thousands.
Landmark laptops.Toshiba T1100: Often called the first mass-market laptop, it ran on batteries.
Landmark laptops.PowerBook 100: Apple pushed the keyboard back and left room for palm rests, a layout now standard.
Landmark laptops.ThinkPad 700C: IBM's first ThinkPad had a red TrackPoint nub in the keyboard.
Landmark laptops.OLPC XO-1: The hand-cranked, rugged $100 laptop was meant for children in developing countries.
Landmark laptops.MacBook Air: Steve Jobs famously pulled it from a manila envelope on stage.
Landmark laptops.Google Cr-48: Google's unbranded black test machine for Chrome OS was never sold to the public.
Landmark laptops.Surface Pro: Microsoft's tablet with a kickstand and keyboard cover tried to merge two kinds of devices.
Landmark laptops.M1 MacBook Air: Apple's first Mac with its own chip had no fan.

Old currencies: how many made one euro.Maltese lira: The Maltese lira was worth more than a euro, and a single euro was only about 0.43 of one, making it among the strongest currencies in Europe.
Old currencies: how many made one euro.Irish pound: The Irish pound, or punt, was replaced in 2002, and the euro's rate was fixed irrevocably before the notes arrived.
Old currencies: how many made one euro.Deutsche Mark: The Deutsche Mark was the symbol of postwar German recovery, and many Germans were reluctant to give it up.
Old currencies: how many made one euro.Dutch guilder: The Dutch guilder was one of the oldest currencies in Europe, and its name means golden.
Old currencies: how many made one euro.Finnish markka: The Finnish markka dates to 1860 and was the national currency until the euro replaced it.
Old currencies: how many made one euro.French franc: The French franc dates to the 14th century, and old francs were exchangeable for euros until 2012.
Old currencies: how many made one euro.Austrian schilling: The Austrian schilling was replaced in 2002, and its notes featured composers and scientists.
Old currencies: how many made one euro.Belgian franc: The Belgian franc was used alongside Luxembourg's franc, and both were replaced at the same rate.
Old currencies: how many made one euro.Spanish peseta: The Spanish peseta was Spain's currency for over a century, and it took about 166 of them to make a euro.
Old currencies: how many made one euro.Italian lira: The Italian lira was so low in value that it took nearly 2,000 of them to make a single euro, and Italians counted in millions.

Beatles songs by release year.Love Me Do: Love Me Do was the Beatles' first single, and it reached number 17 in the UK charts.
Beatles songs by release year.She Loves You: She Loves You is the band's best-selling UK single, and its yeah yeah yeah chorus defined the sound of Beatlemania.
Beatles songs by release year.Can't Buy Me Love: Can't Buy Me Love was written by McCartney, and its opening chorus was unusual for a pop song at the time.
Beatles songs by release year.Yesterday: Yesterday is among the most covered songs in history, and McCartney reportedly dreamed the melody.
Beatles songs by release year.Eleanor Rigby: Eleanor Rigby features a string octet and no band instruments, and it tells a bleak story of loneliness.
Beatles songs by release year.All You Need Is Love: All You Need Is Love was broadcast live to an estimated 400 million people worldwide, in the first global TV link-up.
Beatles songs by release year.Hey Jude: Hey Jude runs over seven minutes, and it was unusually long for a single, and it topped the charts anyway.
Beatles songs by release year.Come Together: Come Together opens Abbey Road, and its bassline is among the best known, and it was written for a political campaign.
Beatles songs by release year.Let It Be: Let It Be was written by McCartney after he dreamed of his mother, and it was released as the band was splitting up.
Beatles songs by release year.Free as a Bird: Free as a Bird was built from a John Lennon demo recorded in the 1970s, and the surviving Beatles finished it in 1995.

How hot is it?.Human body: The textbook 37 degrees dates from the 1800s; studies suggest the average body temperature has dropped slightly since.
How hot is it?.Death Valley record: Recorded at Furnace Creek in 1913, it is still the official highest air temperature ever measured.
How hot is it?.Boiling water: It boils at 100 only at sea level; on Everest's summit, water boils around 70 degrees.
How hot is it?.Kitchen oven, max: Self-cleaning cycles go far hotter, roughly 450 to 500 degrees, turning leftover grime into ash.
How hot is it?.Surface of Venus: Its thick carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat so well that it's hotter than Mercury, even though Mercury is closer to the Sun.
How hot is it?.Flowing lava: Glowing orange basaltic lava, as in Hawaii, typically flows at around 1,000 to 1,200 degrees.
How hot is it?.Light bulb filament: Tungsten, with the highest melting point of any metal at about 3,400 degrees, is why bulbs use it.
How hot is it?.Surface of the Sun: Above this visible surface, the Sun's outer atmosphere, the corona, is millions of degrees hotter, a long-standing puzzle.
How hot is it?.Lightning bolt: A lightning bolt is several times hotter than the Sun's surface, though only for a tiny fraction of a second.
How hot is it?.Core of the Sun: Hydrogen fusing into helium here powers the Sun, and the light then takes tens of thousands of years to escape.

Big numbers, from big to unimaginable.Hundred: The Latin root 'centum' gives us century, cent and percent, since percent literally means per hundred.
Big numbers, from big to unimaginable.Thousand: The Greek 'khilioi' gives the prefix kilo-, which is why a kilometer is a thousand meters and a kilogram a thousand grams.
Big numbers, from big to unimaginable.Million: A million seconds is only about 11.5 days, though a million feels far larger when it's applied to money.
Big numbers, from big to unimaginable.Billion: A billion seconds is about 31.7 years, and Britain once used 'billion' for a million million, switching to the US meaning in the 1970s.
Big numbers, from big to unimaginable.Trillion: A trillion seconds is nearly 32,000 years, which is far longer than recorded history, and so is hard to picture.
Big numbers, from big to unimaginable.Quadrillion: A 2022 study estimated about 20 quadrillion ants live on Earth, which is roughly 2.5 million ants for every human.
Big numbers, from big to unimaginable.Quintillion: A popular back-of-envelope estimate puts the grains of sand on all Earth's beaches at about 7.5 quintillion.
Big numbers, from big to unimaginable.Sextillion: Astronomers estimate that the observable universe holds roughly 10 to 1,000 sextillion stars, more than all the sand grains on Earth.
Big numbers, from big to unimaginable.Googol: Mathematician Edward Kasner's nine-year-old nephew coined it in 1920, and a misspelling of it gave Google its name.
Big numbers, from big to unimaginable.Googolplex: Writing this number in ordinary digits is impossible, since the observable universe has only about 10^80 atoms, far too few to hold its zeros.

One 1990s hit per year: put them in orde.Terminator 2: Terminator 2 pioneered computer-generated liquid metal for the T-1000 and became the highest-grossing film of 1991.
One 1990s hit per year: put them in orde.Aladdin: Aladdin gave Robin Williams the Genie, and his rapid-fire improvisation meant the team used only a fraction of the lines he recorded.
One 1990s hit per year: put them in orde.Jurassic Park: Jurassic Park's dinosaurs combined animatronics by Stan Winston and groundbreaking CGI, and the T. rex roar blends animal sounds including elephant.
One 1990s hit per year: put them in orde.Forrest Gump: Forrest Gump won six Oscars including Best Picture, and Tom Hanks's famous box of chocolates line is among the most quoted movie lines.
One 1990s hit per year: put them in orde.Toy Story: Toy Story was the first entirely computer-animated feature film and launched Pixar's string of hits.
One 1990s hit per year: put them in orde.Independence Day: Independence Day made a worldwide splash with its alien-invasion destruction, and its release on July 4th weekend was perfectly timed.
One 1990s hit per year: put them in orde.Titanic: Titanic became the first film to earn over a billion dollars and tied the record with 11 Oscars, including Best Picture.
One 1990s hit per year: put them in orde.The Truman Show: The Truman Show imagined a man whose entire life was a television broadcast, a premise that predicted reality TV and social media.
One 1990s hit per year: put them in orde.The Matrix: The Matrix introduced 'bullet time' camera effects and helped popularize the red pill as a cultural shorthand.

When these internet companies were found.Amazon: It began selling books from Jeff Bezos's garage in Seattle, and was named for the world's largest river to suggest scale.
When these internet companies were found.eBay: The first item sold, a broken laser pointer, went for $14.83, and the founder was so surprised he emailed the buyer to check.
When these internet companies were found.Netflix: It began by mailing DVDs, and Blockbuster reportedly passed on a chance to buy it, only to go bankrupt later.
When these internet companies were found.Google: It began as BackRub, and the final name comes from googol, the number 1 followed by a hundred zeros.
When these internet companies were found.Skype: Founded by Niklas Zennstrom and Janus Friis, with its software developed by engineers in Estonia, and later bought by Microsoft.
When these internet companies were found.Spotify: Founded in Stockholm by Daniel Ek and Martin Lorentzon, the streaming service was built to compete with music piracy.
When these internet companies were found.Airbnb: It began when its founders rented out air mattresses in a San Francisco apartment, and they sold cereal boxes to stay afloat.
When these internet companies were found.Uber: It began as UberCab, summoned by text message, in San Francisco, before the app became its main way to book rides.
When these internet companies were found.Zoom: Its use rose from about 10 million daily users to over 300 million in a few months of the 2020 pandemic.
When these internet companies were found.Discord: It began as a chat tool made by a team whose game, Fates Forever, flopped, and was aimed at gamers talking while they play.

European capitals from west to east.Lisbon: The westernmost mainland capital of Europe, Lisbon was devastated by a huge earthquake and tsunami in 1755 and rebuilt on a grid.
European capitals from west to east.Dublin: The name comes from the Irish dubh linn, meaning black pool, the tidal pool where the River Poddle met the Liffey.
European capitals from west to east.Madrid: It became the capital in 1561 under Philip II, mainly because of its central location, and has stayed so since, except a few years.
European capitals from west to east.London: The prime meridian passes through Greenwich, so London straddles zero longitude, with just a bit lying to the east.
European capitals from west to east.Paris: France used the Paris meridian as zero until 1911, and a line of brass markers in the pavement still traces it.
European capitals from west to east.Oslo: It burned down in 1624 and was rebuilt as Christiania, a name it kept until 1925.
European capitals from west to east.Rome: The independent Vatican City lies entirely within Rome, making it a country inside a capital.
European capitals from west to east.Stockholm: The city is built on 14 islands linked by bridges, where Lake Malaren meets the Baltic Sea.
European capitals from west to east.Athens: Named for the goddess Athena, according to legend after she beat Poseidon in a contest to be the city's patron.
European capitals from west to east.Moscow: It is the most populous city entirely in Europe, and its Metro stations are famous for ornate halls.

Grand Canyon rock layers, from the river.Vishnu Schist: This dark rock at the canyon's bottom is the base of ancient mountain ranges, squeezed and baked into schist deep underground.
Grand Canyon rock layers, from the river.Tapeats Sandstone: A tough cliff-forming sandstone, deposited when a sea crept across the land, it marks the base of the Tonto Group.
Grand Canyon rock layers, from the river.Bright Angel Shale: Named for a creek, this soft shale forms the broad Tonto Platform where trails flatten, and holds trilobite fossils.
Grand Canyon rock layers, from the river.Muav Limestone: It formed in a calm shallow sea, and with Tapeats and Bright Angel forms the Tonto Group; it is named for a side canyon.
Grand Canyon rock layers, from the river.Redwall Limestone: The grey limestone cliff is stained red by iron-rich mud washed down from the layers above, and is about 150 metres thick.
Grand Canyon rock layers, from the river.Supai Group: These red layers preserve reptile footprints from an age when this region was a vast, hot floodplain near the coast.
Grand Canyon rock layers, from the river.Hermit Shale: A soft red shale named for the Hermit Trail, it holds fossil ferns and the tracks of early reptiles.
Grand Canyon rock layers, from the river.Coconino Sandstone: Its pale, slanted layers are ancient dunes, from a desert like the Sahara, and preserve fossil footprints of animals walking across.
Grand Canyon rock layers, from the river.Toroweap Formation: A thin and mixed band of limestone and sandstone, named after the Toroweap Valley, it sits between two much more famous layers.
Grand Canyon rock layers, from the river.Kaibab Limestone: The rim layer holds fossils of sea creatures, like sponges and shells, proof that the high plateau was once under water.

Roman emperors, in order of reign.Augustus: Born Octavian, he reportedly boasted that he found Rome a city of brick and left it in marble.
Roman emperors, in order of reign.Tiberius: He spent his last decade on the island of Capri, ruling the empire from afar.
Roman emperors, in order of reign.Caligula: His real name was Gaius; 'Caligula' means 'little boots', a nickname from the soldier-style sandals he wore as a child.
Roman emperors, in order of reign.Claudius: Overlooked for years because of physical ailments, he turned out to be a scholar and added Britain to the empire in 43.
Roman emperors, in order of reign.Nero: He died at 30 in 68 AD; the tale of fiddling while Rome burned is myth, as fiddles did not exist yet.
Roman emperors, in order of reign.Vespasian: He began building the Colosseum, and French public urinals are called 'vespasiennes' after his urine tax.
Roman emperors, in order of reign.Trajan: Under him the empire reached its greatest extent, and a carved column in Rome still tells his Dacian wars.
Roman emperors, in order of reign.Hadrian: His wall across northern Britain still stands, and he rebuilt the Pantheon.
Roman emperors, in order of reign.Marcus Aurelius: This philosopher emperor wrote his private Meditations in Greek, partly while on military campaign.
Roman emperors, in order of reign.Constantine the Great: He legalized Christianity across the empire and founded Constantinople, later Istanbul.

Decathlon events in competition order.100 m: The race starts the decathlon and earns the winner the nickname 'world's greatest athlete'.
Decathlon events in competition order.Long jump: In the decathlon, competitors get only three attempts, not six.
Decathlon events in competition order.Shot put: Athletes throw a heavy 7.26 kilogram ball, testing raw power early on.
Decathlon events in competition order.High jump: Three misses in a row at any height and the athlete is out of the event.
Decathlon events in competition order.400 m: A lung-burning lap ends the first day, leaving athletes exhausted before sleep.
Decathlon events in competition order.110 m hurdles: For decathletes the hurdles stand about 1.07 meters high.
Decathlon events in competition order.Discus: Athletes throw from a circle about 2.5 meters across, spinning to build speed.
Decathlon events in competition order.Pole vault: A single failure to clear any height can score zero points, making this one of the most dreaded events.
Decathlon events in competition order.Javelin: The spear weighs about 800 grams, and a long throw requires a smooth run-up.
Decathlon events in competition order.1500 m: The final race is a long grind, and its result often decides the overall standings.

Bond and Batman actors by debut year.Sean Connery as Bond: Dr. No made Connery a star; Ian Fleming doubted the Scot at first, but later gave Bond a Scottish father in the books.
Bond and Batman actors by debut year.Adam West as Batman: His campy 1966 TV series lasted just three seasons, yet its Pow! fight captions and the Batusi dance became pop icons.
Bond and Batman actors by debut year.George Lazenby as Bond: A model with no acting experience, he starred in On Her Majesty's Secret Service and quit after one film, against advice.
Bond and Batman actors by debut year.Roger Moore as Bond: He played Bond seven times, more than anyone else, from Live and Let Die to A View to a Kill at age 57.
Bond and Batman actors by debut year.Timothy Dalton as Bond: A trained Shakespearean actor, he aimed for a darker, Fleming-style Bond, but legal disputes stalled the series after just two films.
Bond and Batman actors by debut year.Michael Keaton as Batman: Fans protested casting a comedy actor as the Dark Knight, but Tim Burton's film was a smash hit.
Bond and Batman actors by debut year.George Clooney as Batman: Batman & Robin, with its infamous rubber suits, was a critical flop, and Clooney has joked about it for years.
Bond and Batman actors by debut year.Christian Bale as Batman: Batman Begins rebooted the hero in a realistic tone, and the follow-up, The Dark Knight, won Heath Ledger a posthumous Oscar.
Bond and Batman actors by debut year.Daniel Craig as Bond: Fans protested his blond hair, but Casino Royale was a hit; he played Bond five times, ending with No Time to Die.
Bond and Batman actors by debut year.Robert Pattinson as Batman: His reclusive, detective-style Bruce Wayne in a gritty noir came years after he starred in the Twilight films.

Stop-motion animated films by release.A Grand Day Out: Nick Park's first Wallace and Gromit film sends them to a cheese-filled Moon, and took about six years to make.
Stop-motion animated films by release.James and the Giant Peach: Directed by Henry Selick, it blends live action with stop-motion in an adaptation of Roald Dahl's book.
Stop-motion animated films by release.Chicken Run: Aardman's first feature became the highest-grossing stop-motion film ever made.
Stop-motion animated films by release.Corpse Bride: Tim Burton co-directed it with Mike Johnson, and it was nominated for an Oscar for Best Animated Feature.
Stop-motion animated films by release.Coraline: Laika's first film, adapted from Neil Gaiman's novella, features handmade button eyes.
Stop-motion animated films by release.ParaNorman: Laika used thousands of 3D-printed faces to give its characters their expressions.
Stop-motion animated films by release.The Boxtrolls: Laika again, adapting Alan Snow's novel Here Be Monsters!, about trolls living beneath Cheesebridge.
Stop-motion animated films by release.Kubo and the Two Strings: It features a 16-foot-tall skeleton puppet, the largest stop-motion puppet ever built.
Stop-motion animated films by release.Missing Link: Laika's Bigfoot tale, voiced by Hugh Jackman and Zach Galifianakis, won the Golden Globe for Best Animated Feature.
Stop-motion animated films by release.Vengeance Most Fowl: Wallace and Gromit return, with the penguin villain Feathers McGraw, last seen in 1993's The Wrong Trousers.

Dinosaur timeline: who came first?.Herrerasaurus: One of the oldest known dinosaurs, a nimble meat-eater from Argentina, it was a few meters long.
Dinosaur timeline: who came first?.Coelophysis: This small, slender predator from North America was found in huge numbers at Ghost Ranch, New Mexico, and a skull of one flew on the space shuttle.
Dinosaur timeline: who came first?.Scelidosaurus: This armored plant-eater from Britain was among the first dinosaurs with body armor, and it may have been an early ancestor of ankylosaurs.
Dinosaur timeline: who came first?.Megalosaurus: The first dinosaur ever named, in 1824, from bones found near Oxford, and it was first thought to be a giant lizard.
Dinosaur timeline: who came first?.Allosaurus: Allosaurus was a top predator of the Jurassic, and its fossils show it had healed injuries, so it lived a tough life.
Dinosaur timeline: who came first?.Baryonyx: Baryonyx had a long crocodile-like snout and large thumb claw, and it may have eaten fish.
Dinosaur timeline: who came first?.Ouranosaurus: Ouranosaurus was an African plant-eater with a sail-like ridge on its back, perhaps used to regulate heat.
Dinosaur timeline: who came first?.Argentinosaurus: Argentinosaurus was an enormous Argentine sauropod, perhaps dozens of tonnes, and is among the largest land animals known.
Dinosaur timeline: who came first?.Parasaurolophus: The crest on this duckbill's head was a hollow tube that was probably used to make deep, resonant calls.
Dinosaur timeline: who came first?.Triceratops: The three-horned dinosaur lived until the very end of the Cretaceous, and it's among the last dinosaurs before the asteroid impact.

Russian classics, by publication.Eugene Onegin: Pushkin's novel in verse became the basis for Tchaikovsky's opera, and Pushkin died in a duel.
Russian classics, by publication.Dead Souls: Gogol's satire follows a swindler buying up dead serfs' names, and it was meant to be part of a trilogy.
Russian classics, by publication.Fathers and Sons: Turgenev's novel popularized the word nihilist through its character Bazarov.
Russian classics, by publication.Crime and Punishment: Dostoevsky's novel follows Raskolnikov, a student who commits murder, and it's one of literature's great psychological studies.
Russian classics, by publication.War and Peace: Tolstoy's epic follows several aristocratic families through Napoleon's invasion of Russia and has hundreds of characters.
Russian classics, by publication.Anna Karenina: This tragic novel opens with the line about unhappy families, and it begins with a famous train station scene.
Russian classics, by publication.The Brothers Karamazov: Dostoevsky's last novel was published in a magazine, and he died only months after it was completed.
Russian classics, by publication.Doctor Zhivago: Pasternak's novel was banned in the USSR, and he was forced to decline the Nobel Prize in 1958.
Solzhenitsyn's novella about a prison camp was published under Khrushchev, and it changed Soviet literature.
Russian classics, by publication.The Master and Margarita: Bulgakov's satirical fantasy about the Devil visiting Moscow was only published about 25 years after his death.

Air pressure: from thin air to record hi.Kármán line: At 100 km up, this is the conventional boundary between Earth's atmosphere and space, set by the point where wings stop working.
Air pressure: from thin air to record hi.50 km up: Only about a thousandth of surface pressure remains, so a weather balloon bursts long before it climbs this high.
Air pressure: from thin air to record hi.19 km up (Armstrong limit): Above this altitude, water in a person's body would boil at body temperature, so pilots need pressurised suits.
Air pressure: from thin air to record hi.Summit of Everest: The air has about a third of sea-level pressure, which is why most climbers use bottled oxygen.
Air pressure: from thin air to record hi.Summit of Mont Blanc: At 4,808 m, the highest peak in the Alps has air pressure of roughly half that at sea level.
Air pressure: from thin air to record hi.Denver: Thin air in the 'Mile High City' sends baseballs flying farther, so Coors Field stores baseballs in a humidor.
Air pressure: from thin air to record hi.Eye of Typhoon Tip: In 1979 this became the lowest sea-level pressure ever recorded. It was also the largest tropical cyclone ever measured, about 2,200 km across.
Air pressure: from thin air to record hi.Standard sea level: The air above each square metre weighs around ten tonnes, and we don't feel it because our bodies push back.
Air pressure: from thin air to record hi.Dead Sea shore: It's Earth's lowest dry land, about 430 m below sea level, so the air is slightly thicker and richer in oxygen.
Air pressure: from thin air to record hi.Record high (Agata, Siberia): A bitter cold snap in December 1968 produced the highest sea-level pressure ever recorded at this remote Russian village.

Latin-rooted -ary words, by the number i.Primary: The word comes from Latin primus, 'first'. It is why the first school years are called primary and why the first colours of paint are called primary colours.
Latin-rooted -ary words, by the number i.Secondary: From Latin secundus, 'following', the word originally meant 'second in line', which is also the root of the time unit second.
Latin-rooted -ary words, by the number i.Tertiary: Tertiary comes from Latin tertius, 'third', and it appears in geology: the Tertiary period was the third era in an old scheme, now split up.
Latin-rooted -ary words, by the number i.Quaternary: Quaternary is the name of the geologic period we live in now, which began about 2.6 million years ago and covers the ice ages.
Latin-rooted -ary words, by the number i.Quinary: Quinary means based on five, and some old counting systems used it; the Roman numeral V is thought to depict a hand with five fingers.
Latin-rooted -ary words, by the number i.Senary: Senary means counted in sixes, and a base-six number system is seen as very compact, since six divides evenly by both 2 and 3.
Latin-rooted -ary words, by the number i.Septenary: The word is rare, yet septenary works as an old term for the number seven, such as the seven days of a week or the seven classical planets.
Latin-rooted -ary words, by the number i.Octonary: Octonary means made of eight, and it is the less common sibling of octal, the base-eight system once beloved by computer programmers.
Latin-rooted -ary words, by the number i.Nonary: Nonary means counting in nines, and its base is also known as base-nine; it echoes Latin novem, which is where November got its name.
Latin-rooted -ary words, by the number i.Denary: Denary is simply our everyday decimal system, base ten, and the word comes from Latin deni, 'ten each'.

Milestones by women in medicine.Blackwell becomes a US doctor: Elizabeth Blackwell, born in England, finished first in her class at a New York college that had admitted her as a joke.
Milestones by women in medicine.Nightingale goes to Crimea: Florence Nightingale cut death rates in military hospitals, and used pioneering statistical charts to persuade officials.
Milestones by women in medicine.Barton founds US Red Cross: Clara Barton had earned the nickname 'angel of the battlefield' tending the wounded in the Civil War.
Milestones by women in medicine.Marie Curie's first Nobel: She shared the 1903 physics prize for radioactivity, and won again in chemistry in 1911, the only person honoured in two different sciences.
Milestones by women in medicine.Sanger's birth control clinic: Margaret Sanger opened the first such clinic in the US in Brooklyn, and was arrested within days.
Milestones by women in medicine.Apgar's newborn score: Virginia Apgar's quick test is still given to babies at one and five minutes, and its name doubles as a memory aid for its five checks.
Milestones by women in medicine.Tu Youyou finds artemisinin: Searching ancient Chinese texts for malaria cures, she isolated the drug from sweet wormwood, and won a Nobel in 2015.
Milestones by women in medicine.Gertrude Elion's Nobel: She never earned a doctorate, yet her drug discoveries covered leukaemia, gout and transplants, and won a share in the 1988 Nobel.
Milestones by women in medicine.Doudna's CRISPR paper: Jennifer Doudna and Emmanuelle Charpentier showed bacterial defences could be used as gene-editing scissors, and won the 2020 Nobel in Chemistry.
Milestones by women in medicine.Karikó's Nobel: Katalin Karikó was demoted at her university for her mRNA work, which later made COVID vaccines possible.

When these ancient empires fell.Akkadian Empire: Founded by Sargon of Akkad, it is often called the first empire in history, ruling the cities of Mesopotamia from one throne.
When these ancient empires fell.Hittite Empire: After a huge battle at Kadesh against Egypt, it signed what is regarded as the oldest surviving peace treaty, and a copy hangs at the UN.
When these ancient empires fell.Neo-Assyrian Empire: Its capital Nineveh held the library of Ashurbanipal, tens of thousands of clay tablets that preserved the Epic of Gilgamesh.
When these ancient empires fell.Neo-Babylonian Empire: Nebuchadnezzar II built the Ishtar Gate here, and the Hanging Gardens are said to have been made for this empire's capital.
When these ancient empires fell.Achaemenid Persia: Founded by Cyrus the Great, it was the largest empire the world had yet seen, linked by a Royal Road with relay riders.
When these ancient empires fell.Maurya Empire: Its emperor Ashoka, after a bloody war at Kalinga, turned to Buddhism and carved his edicts on pillars across India.
When these ancient empires fell.Carthage: Rome razed the city at the end of the Third Punic War; the story that Romans sowed the ground with salt is probably a later legend.
When these ancient empires fell.Seleucid Empire: Carved from Alexander's conquests by Seleucus I, it ruled from Syria; a revolt against it is the story behind Hanukkah.
When these ancient empires fell.Han dynasty: Under the Han, the Silk Road opened to the west, and Chinese people still call themselves the Han people today.
When these ancient empires fell.Gupta Empire: Often called India's golden age, this era saw mathematician Aryabhata work and the decimal system with zero take shape.

Fantasy novels, by publication year.The Hobbit: Tolkien reportedly scribbled its famous first line, about a hobbit in a hole in the ground, on a blank page while marking exam papers.
C. S. Lewis's book opened the seven-volume Chronicles of Narnia; his friend Tolkien reportedly disliked its mix of myths and talking animals.
Fantasy novels, by publication year.The Fellowship of the Ring: The Lord of the Rings was written as one story; the publisher split it into three volumes because of its length and postwar costs.
Fantasy novels, by publication year.A Wizard of Earthsea: Ursula K. Le Guin's novel features a wizard school years before Hogwarts, and the idea that knowing a thing's true name gives power over it.
Fantasy novels, by publication year.The Colour of Magic: Terry Pratchett's first Discworld novel introduced a flat world carried on four elephants standing on the shell of the giant turtle Great A'Tuin.
Fantasy novels, by publication year.The Eye of the World: Robert Jordan's opener began The Wheel of Time, so long that Brandon Sanderson completed it after Jordan died in 2007.
Fantasy novels, by publication year.A Game of Thrones: George R. R. Martin's novel began A Song of Ice and Fire, the series that inspired the HBO hit Game of Thrones starting in 2011.
Fantasy novels, by publication year.Harry Potter (first book): Rejected by many publishers before it was accepted, the first Potter book was retitled Sorcerer's Stone in the US, since philosopher sounded dull.
Fantasy novels, by publication year.Mistborn: Brandon Sanderson's series runs on allomancy, a magic system in which people gain powers by swallowing and burning different metals.
Fantasy novels, by publication year.The Name of the Wind: Patrick Rothfuss's debut tells of Kvothe, a gifted musician and arcanist, and opens The Kingkiller Chronicle, a planned trilogy.

Golf clubs by typical loft.Driver: Its low loft and big head, capped at 460 cubic centimetres, are built to send the ball as far as possible.
Golf clubs by typical loft.3-wood: Useful off the tee or fairway, it is harder to hit cleanly from the ground than a driver off a tee.
Golf clubs by typical loft.5-wood: Its wide, shallow sole glides through the grass, so many players find it friendlier than a long iron.
Golf clubs by typical loft.3-iron: Lee Trevino joked that even God can't hit a one-iron; many players have swapped long irons for hybrids.
Golf clubs by typical loft.5-iron: Modern irons have stronger lofts than old ones, so today's 5-iron flies about as far as a classic 4-iron.
Golf clubs by typical loft.7-iron: Mid-set, it balances distance and control, and is often the club beginners are taught on first.
Golf clubs by typical loft.9-iron: Short irons launch the ball high with lots of backspin, so it lands softly and stops quickly on the green.
Golf clubs by typical loft.Pitching wedge: Named for pitch shots, it usually comes with the iron set rather than being bought separately.
Golf clubs by typical loft.Sand wedge: Gene Sarazen is credited with adding a flange to the sole in the 1930s so the club bounces out of bunkers instead of digging.
Golf clubs by typical loft.Lob wedge: With the highest loft in most bags, it can pop the ball almost straight up for short shots over obstacles.

The lowest note each instrument can play.Piano: At 27.5 hertz, it is the lowest key of an 88-key piano.
The lowest note each instrument can play.Contrabassoon: It sounds an octave below the bassoon, and its folded tube is about five metres long.
The lowest note each instrument can play.Double bass: Its strings are tuned in fourths, and some orchestral basses extend down to C1 with extra length.
The lowest note each instrument can play.Bassoon: A double-reed instrument whose folded tube is roughly 2.5 metres long. It is sometimes called the clown of the orchestra.
The lowest note each instrument can play.Cello: Its lowest string, C2, is two octaves below middle C. Bach wrote six famous suites for the unaccompanied instrument.
The lowest note each instrument can play.Viola: Tuned a fifth below the violin, giving it the same notes as the cello's upper strings, an octave higher.
The lowest note each instrument can play.Violin: Its lowest string, G3, is the G below middle C. Stradivari's violins are among the most valuable instruments.
The lowest note each instrument can play.Oboe: The orchestra tunes to its A, because its pitch is steady and hard to alter.
The lowest note each instrument can play.Flute: The modern flute is metal but still counted a woodwind, as it makes sound without a reed.
The lowest note each instrument can play.Piccolo: It sounds an octave above written pitch, which is why its notes are written lower than they sound.

Mediterranean islands by area.Capri: The Roman emperor Tiberius ruled from a villa here, and its Blue Grotto glows because sunlight enters through an underwater opening.
Mediterranean islands by area.Malta (main island): Home to temples older than the pyramids, this island is part of an independent country, and it was ruled by the Knights of St John.
Mediterranean islands by area.Ibiza: The island's old walled town, Dalt Vila, is a UNESCO site, though it is better known for its nightclubs.
Mediterranean islands by area.Menorca: This island is a Biosphere Reserve, and Mahón, its capital, is said to have given mayonnaise its name.
Mediterranean islands by area.Rhodes: The Colossus, a giant statue about 30 m tall and one of the Seven Wonders, stood here until an earthquake toppled it.
Mediterranean islands by area.Mallorca: Composer Chopin spent a rainy winter here in 1838, and it's the largest of Spain's Balearic Islands.
Mediterranean islands by area.Crete: Home of the Minoans, Europe's first advanced civilization, with a palace at Knossos linked to the legend of the Minotaur.
Mediterranean islands by area.Cyprus: Its name is linked to copper, which was mined here in ancient times, and it's said to be the birthplace of Aphrodite.
Mediterranean islands by area.Sardinia: Dotted with thousands of stone towers called nuraghi, it's also known as one of the world's regions with the most centenarians.
Mediterranean islands by area.Sicily: The largest island in the Mediterranean, it has Mount Etna, Europe's most active volcano, and was the home of Archimedes.

When these spacecraft blasted off.Pioneer 10: It was the first craft to cross the asteroid belt and fly past Jupiter, and it carried a plaque showing humankind's location.
When these spacecraft blasted off.Viking 1: The first US Mars lander to work, it spent years sending pictures from the surface and ran biology tests searching for life.
When these spacecraft blasted off.Voyager 1: The farthest human-made object, it entered interstellar space in 2012 carrying a golden record of Earth's sounds.
When these spacecraft blasted off.Galileo (to Jupiter): It orbited Jupiter for eight years and found signs of a hidden ocean under the ice of the moon Europa.
When these spacecraft blasted off.Cassini–Huygens: The Huygens probe parachuted onto Saturn's moon Titan, and Cassini ended in 2017 by plunging into Saturn on purpose.
When these spacecraft blasted off.New Horizons: It reached Pluto in 2015, and it carries a small portion of the ashes of Clyde Tombaugh, who discovered Pluto.
When these spacecraft blasted off.Kepler space telescope: It spent years watching one patch of sky for planets passing in front of their stars, finding thousands of worlds.
When these spacecraft blasted off.Curiosity rover: A car-sized rover that landed using a rocket-powered sky crane, it explores Gale Crater and found ancient lakebed clues.
When these spacecraft blasted off.Perseverance rover: It brought along the Ingenuity helicopter, which made the first powered flight on another planet in 2021.
When these spacecraft blasted off.James Webb Space Telescope: It launched on Christmas Day 2021 and flew to a point 1.5 million km from Earth, and it sees the earliest galaxies.

How many sides or faces?.Yield sign: The only US road sign shaped like a downward-pointing triangle, which makes it stand out among signs.
How many sides or faces?.Playing card: Poker-size cards measure 2.5 by 3.5 inches, while bridge cards are slightly narrower.
How many sides or faces?.US school-zone sign: Fluorescent yellow-green and shaped like a house, it is the pentagon drivers see near schools.
How many sides or faces?.Hex nut: Six sides let a wrench grip from several angles in tight spaces, which is why most nuts are hexagonal.
How many sides or faces?.UK 50p coin: A curved heptagon of constant width, so it rolls through vending machines just like a round coin.
How many sides or faces?.Stop sign: The octagon was chosen so it can be recognized from behind or when covered in snow.
How many sides or faces?.Canadian loonie: Canada's one-dollar coin is nicknamed for the bird on its back and replaced the paper note in 1987.
How many sides or faces?.UK £1 coin: The 12-sided coin entered circulation in 2017 with security features like a hologram-style image, replacing the round pound.
How many sides or faces?.Die inside a Magic 8-Ball: Inside floats a 20-sided icosahedron with answers: ten affirmative, five noncommittal and five negative.
How many sides or faces?.Classic soccer ball panels: The pattern is a truncated icosahedron with 12 pentagons and 20 hexagons, the same shape as a buckyball carbon molecule.

The story of the Nobel Prize, in order.Alfred Nobel is born: Born in Stockholm, the chemist went on to hold 355 patents in his lifetime.
The story of the Nobel Prize, in order.Nobel patents dynamite: Nobel tamed unstable nitroglycerin by mixing it with absorbent clay, making it safe enough to ship.
The story of the Nobel Prize, in order.Nobel signs his will: Signed in Paris, it left most of his fortune to fund prizes, which stunned his relatives.
The story of the Nobel Prize, in order.Alfred Nobel dies: He died in San Remo, Italy, and never saw the prizes; his will named five fields in 1895.
The story of the Nobel Prize, in order.First prizes awarded: Wilhelm Rontgen won the first physics prize for discovering X-rays.
The story of the Nobel Prize, in order.Marie Curie: first woman: She shared the physics prize with Pierre Curie and Henri Becquerel for work on radioactivity.
The story of the Nobel Prize, in order.Curie wins a second prize: The chemistry prize for discovering radium and polonium made her the first person to win in two scientific fields.
The story of the Nobel Prize, in order.Einstein's prize year: His physics prize, awarded in 1922 for the 1921 year, was for the photoelectric effect, not relativity.
The story of the Nobel Prize, in order.Economics prize created: Not one of Nobel's original prizes, it was created by Sweden's central bank, formally in memory of Alfred Nobel.
The story of the Nobel Prize, in order.Malala: youngest laureate: She won at 17 with Kailash Satyarthi, for fighting for children's right to education.

When these medieval scholars were born.Al-Khwarizmi: The Persian polymath's name gave us the word algorithm, and al-jabr in his book title gave us algebra.
When these medieval scholars were born.Al-Kindi: He worked in Baghdad's House of Wisdom and pioneered cryptanalysis through frequency analysis.
When these medieval scholars were born.Al-Razi: A physician in Baghdad who distinguished smallpox from measles, writing the first clear description.
When these medieval scholars were born.Ibn al-Haytham: His Book of Optics showed that we see by light entering the eye, and pioneered experimental method.
When these medieval scholars were born.Omar Khayyam: Remembered as the poet of the Rubaiyat, he was also a mathematician and astronomer who helped reform the Persian calendar.
When these medieval scholars were born.Averroes: The Andalusian philosopher in Cordoba wrote commentaries on Aristotle that earned him the title The Commentator.
When these medieval scholars were born.Rumi: The Persian poet's Masnavi still sells widely, and his followers founded the whirling dervish order.
When these medieval scholars were born.Ibn Battuta: The Moroccan traveler journeyed some 120,000 km across Africa and Asia over about 30 years.
When these medieval scholars were born.Ibn Khaldun: His Muqaddimah is an early work of sociology and economic history, written in the 1370s.
When these medieval scholars were born.Ulugh Beg: The Timurid ruler built a great observatory in Samarkand and catalogued nearly 1,000 stars.

South American capitals from north to so.Caracas: Simón Bolívar was born in this city, which sits in a valley between mountains and the Caribbean coast.
South American capitals from north to so.Georgetown: Its St George's Cathedral is among the tallest wooden churches in the world.
South American capitals from north to so.Paramaribo: A mosque and a synagogue stand side by side in this UNESCO-listed historic centre.
South American capitals from north to so.Bogotá: It sits on a high plateau about 2,600 m above sea level.
South American capitals from north to so.Quito: At about 2,850 m, it is one of the highest capitals, and lies only a short distance from the equator.
South American capitals from north to so.Lima: One of the world's largest desert cities, it gets almost no rain, though it's humid from ocean fog.
South American capitals from north to so.La Paz: The highest seat of government in the world, at around 3,600 m, with commuter cable cars.
South American capitals from north to so.Asunción: Called 'Mother of Cities', since expeditions set out from here to found other cities, including Buenos Aires.
South American capitals from north to so.Santiago: Snow-capped Andes peaks loom over the city, and Chile's capital sits in a valley.
South American capitals from north to so.Buenos Aires: Its residents are called porteños, 'people of the port', and tango was born around its docks.

Actors who first played the Doctor in Do.William Hartnell: William Hartnell was the first Doctor, and he was already an established film actor who was cast at 55.
Actors who first played the Doctor in Do.Patrick Troughton: Patrick Troughton took over in 1966 and invented the idea of regeneration, which let the show carry on with new actors.
Actors who first played the Doctor in Do.Jon Pertwee: Jon Pertwee's Doctor was stuck on Earth for a time and he often performed his own stunts, and loved gadgets and vehicles.
Actors who first played the Doctor in Do.Tom Baker: Tom Baker is the longest-serving Doctor, with seven years, and his long scarf became a famous symbol.
Actors who first played the Doctor in Do.Peter Davison: Peter Davison was just 29 when he was cast, then the youngest actor in the role at that time.
Actors who first played the Doctor in Do.Colin Baker: Colin Baker's Doctor wore a famously multicolored coat, and he only did two seasons before being dismissed.
Actors who first played the Doctor in Do.Sylvester McCoy: Sylvester McCoy played the Doctor during the show's last years of the original run, and he was a stage performer who played spoons.
Actors who first played the Doctor in Do.Paul McGann: Paul McGann appeared in a 1996 TV movie and returned for a mini-episode in 2013, and he is the Eighth Doctor.
Actors who first played the Doctor in Do.Christopher Eccleston: Christopher Eccleston revived the show in 2005 and was the Ninth Doctor, though he stayed for only one season.
Actors who first played the Doctor in Do.Matt Smith: Matt Smith became the youngest Doctor at the time, aged 26, and he led the show's 50th anniversary special.

Web frameworks and libraries by release.Ruby on Rails: David Heinemeier Hansson extracted it from Basecamp, and its 'convention over configuration' idea shaped web development.
Web frameworks and libraries by release.Django: Named for jazz guitarist Django Reinhardt, it was created at a Kansas newspaper to meet tight deadlines.
Web frameworks and libraries by release.jQuery: John Resig's library made the dollar-sign shortcut famous and smoothed over differences between browsers.
Web frameworks and libraries by release.Node.js: Ryan Dahl brought JavaScript to servers using Chrome's V8 engine, which lets the same language run both sides.
Web frameworks and libraries by release.AngularJS: Google's framework began as a side project of Miško Hevery, who rebuilt in weeks what had taken months.
Web frameworks and libraries by release.Bootstrap: It started at Twitter as an in-house design toolkit, first called Blueprint, before going open source.
Web frameworks and libraries by release.React: Facebook's Jordan Walke built it, and developers were at first skeptical about mixing markup into JavaScript with JSX.
Web frameworks and libraries by release.Vue.js: Evan You, a former Google engineer, made it as a lighter alternative, and it grew almost entirely on community support.
Web frameworks and libraries by release.Next.js: It comes from the company Vercel, once called Zeit, and it popularized server-rendered React apps.
Web frameworks and libraries by release.Tailwind CSS: Adam Wathan's 'utility-first' approach put styling in class names, and many first found it ugly, then loved it.

Spotted animals by weight.Ladybird: The spots do not tell its age, a common myth; they differ by species. Its bright colours warn predators that it tastes bad.
Spotted animals by weight.Leopard gecko: This lizard from South Asia can drop its tail to escape a predator, then regrow it. Unlike many geckos, it has eyelids and cannot climb glass.
Spotted animals by weight.Guinea fowl: These spotted African birds are noisy and make good watchdogs on farms. They also eat ticks and many insects.
Spotted animals by weight.Ocelot: This small spotted cat from the Americas has a coat that was once heavily hunted for fur. It hunts mainly at night, often near water.
Spotted animals by weight.Dalmatian: Puppies are born plain white and develop spots after a couple of weeks. The breed ran alongside carriages and later became firehouse mascots.
Spotted animals by weight.Cheetah: The fastest land animal reaches about 100 km/h in short bursts. Its black tear marks reduce sun glare while hunting.
Spotted animals by weight.Jaguar: The largest cat in the Americas has the strongest bite relative to its size among big cats. It often kills by biting through the skull, and likes to swim.
Spotted animals by weight.Appaloosa horse: This breed was developed by the Nez Perce people in North America, and is known for its spotted coat, like a leopard pattern. The name comes from the Palouse River.
Spotted animals by weight.Giraffe: Every giraffe has a unique patch pattern, and a newborn drops about two metres to the ground when born. Giraffes also have just seven neck bones, like humans.
Spotted animals by weight.Whale shark: The largest fish in the world, it feeds only on plankton by filtering seawater. Its spots are unique to each animal, so researchers can identify them.

Charlie and the Chocolate Factory, in or.Augustus Gloop finds a ticket: Roald Dahl's book came out in 1964, and the ticket winners are caricatures of bad habits.
Charlie and the Chocolate Factory, in or.Veruca Salt finds a ticket: Veruca's name echoes verruca, Latin for wart, which suits her spoiled character.
Charlie and the Chocolate Factory, in or.Violet finds a ticket: Dahl wrote the winners as warnings: gluttony, greed, gum-chewing and TV addiction.
Charlie and the Chocolate Factory, in or.Mike Teavee finds a ticket: Mike Teavee is hooked on TV and cowboy films, and Dahl, who criticised television, uses him to mock it.
Charlie and the Chocolate Factory, in or.Charlie finds the last ticket: Charlie is the poorest child in the story, and his ticket comes from a bar bought with a found coin.
Charlie and the Chocolate Factory, in or.Augustus goes up the pipe: Dahl was inspired by Cadbury and Rowntree's rivalry in his school days, when they sent spies to each other's factories.
Charlie and the Chocolate Factory, in or.Violet turns into a blueberry: Violet's gum, Wonka's three-course dinner, is an unfinished invention that goes wrong.
Charlie and the Chocolate Factory, in or.Veruca goes down the chute: The squirrels judge Veruca a bad nut, and she goes down the garbage chute.
Charlie and the Chocolate Factory, in or.Mike is shrunk by television: Wonka's television device sends chocolate through the air, which is how Mike gets shrunk.
Charlie and the Chocolate Factory, in or.Charlie wins the factory: The 1971 film starred Gene Wilder as Wonka, and the 2005 version starred Johnny Depp.

Famous left-handers, by birth year.Leonardo da Vinci: He wrote in mirror script from right to left, probably easier for a left-hander to avoid smudging ink.
Famous left-handers, by birth year.Charlie Chaplin: The Little Tramp's creator was left-handed, and he composed the music for many of his own films.
Famous left-handers, by birth year.Babe Ruth: He began as a left-handed pitcher for Boston before becoming baseball's greatest slugger with the Yankees.
Famous left-handers, by birth year.Ringo Starr: He drums left-handed on a right-handed kit, which gave his fills their distinctive feel.
Famous left-handers, by birth year.Paul McCartney: He plays a left-handed Hofner bass, whose symmetrical violin shape makes it easy to flip.
Famous left-handers, by birth year.Oprah Winfrey: Born in rural Mississippi, she became one of the first Black billionaires.
Famous left-handers, by birth year.Martina Navratilova: Her left-handed serve and volleys won 18 Grand Slam singles titles and a record nine Wimbledon women's titles.
Famous left-handers, by birth year.Barack Obama: Several recent presidents, like Ford, Clinton and George H.W. Bush, were also lefties.
Famous left-handers, by birth year.Tom Cruise: His Mission: Impossible films feature stunts he performs himself, including hanging from a plane.
Famous left-handers, by birth year.Kurt Cobain: The Nirvana frontman played a left-handed guitar, as Jimi Hendrix did by flipping a right-handed Stratocaster.

Daylight on the winter solstice.Longyearbyen: On Svalbard, the sun doesn't rise for months in polar night, yet the town has a cinema, a brewery and a university.
Daylight on the winter solstice.Reykjavik: Iceland's capital gets a short day, with sunrise around 11:20 a.m. and sunset around 3:30 p.m.
Daylight on the winter solstice.Oslo: Norway's capital sees the sun low in the sky, rising around 9 a.m. and setting near 3 p.m.
Daylight on the winter solstice.Moscow: Moscow gets about seven hours of light, with the sun rising nearly at 9 a.m.
Daylight on the winter solstice.London: The solstice sunset draws crowds at Stonehenge, whose stones align with it.
Daylight on the winter solstice.New York: It gets about nine hours of light, and from this day the days begin to lengthen.
Daylight on the winter solstice.Cairo: Even in winter it gets ten hours of light, noticeably shorter than summer's roughly 14.
Daylight on the winter solstice.Singapore: Near the equator, day length barely changes through the year, staying around 12 hours.
Daylight on the winter solstice.Rio de Janeiro: In the southern hemisphere, December begins summer, so this is the longest day of the year.
Daylight on the winter solstice.Sydney: The December solstice is Australia's summer solstice, with sunrise before 5:45 a.m.
